== Summary ==

:{{pov|[[Matrim Cauthon]]}}
As Mat dangles from a balcony three stories up the Tarasin Palace, he consoles himself by thinking that it isn't the hardest place he's ever tried to break into. He makes his way onto the balcony while rehearsing how he will tell [[Fortuona Athaem Devi Paendrag|Tuon]] that [[Lunal Galgan|Galgan]] was betraying her and she should leave the city. 

After reaching her balcony and catching his breath, he goes to enter the room. Before he is through the door, something is shot from the shadows. [[Selucia]] reveals herself to be Tuon's bodyguard as she levels a crossbow at Mat. The two banter, with Selucia very nearly making a joke and coming very close to guessing the reason Mat lost his eye. She dismisses the idea that Galgan would assassinate Tuon and he should be worried more about [[Krisa]], who has hired [[Seanchan]] assassins. She also reminds Mat that the Empress' name is now Fortuona. She shows him a secret passage that will lead to the palace gardens, where Mat will find Tuon. Mat thanks her, although she questions if it is for telling him where Tuon was or not killing him. He replies it is for not calling him "Highness."

:{{pov|[[Rand al'Thor]]}}
Rand walks through [[Elayne Trakand|Elayne's]] camp accompanied by a pair of [[Far Dareis Mai|Maidens]]. Everything in the camp is quiet so as to avoid attracting the [[Trolloc|Trollocs]]. He ruminates on how Elayne asked him to reveal himself when he visits the camp as they fight for him. 

He comes across [[Ban al'Seen]] and [[Dav al'Thone]]. He tells them that they have the most important task: watching over his father. Rand walks into the tent to find his father, [[Tamlin al'Thor|Tam]], looking over maps. Rand presents him with a replacement sword for the one he was unable to return. Tam believes it is too fine, but Rand insists on it being a thank you gift. They discuss the flame and the [[void]] and Tam reveals that it was never about archery or swords. Rather, it is about inner peace. 

The two go outside and Tam convinces his son to duel with him. Rand is hesitant as he hasn't practiced the sword since losing his hand, but Tam wraps a cloth around one of his hands and agrees to duel one-handed, on a level with Rand. Tam has the early advantage, easily out-dueling Rand, who has not practiced sword forms since losing his hand to [[Semirhage]]. Rand quickly becomes frustrated, thinking to himself that he will never be proficient in sword-fighting ever again, and that ''[[saidin]] ''is a much more powerful weapon. Tam continues to test Rand's limits, and Rand grows increasingly resentful of his injury, until he realizes that Tam is also fighting one-handed, and if Tam has overcome this barrier, so can Rand. Taking Tam's advice, he let's go of his emotions, and wins the practice duel.

:{{pov|[[Matrim Cauthon]]}}
Mat makes his way to the gardens. He finds Tuon practicing hand combat forms and admires her beauty from the shadows so as not to distract her. He asks himself if he loves her, but the question makes him uncomfortable. 

Something moves out of the corner of his eye, but he dismisses it as a gardener. He tries to look again and cannot focus on the person that is moving towards Tuon. He steps between the [[Deathwatch Guard]]s and they don't notice him either. Almost unconsciously, he pulls out a knife from his sleeve and throws it at the man, hitting him in the shoulder. Tuon tries to pin down the attacker but misses, as does Mat's second knife, and the [[Gray Man]] escapes. The guards immediately grab Mat and throw him to the ground but Tuon intervenes, telling them to release him and look for the man whose blood is on the ground.  

Mat tells her about Galgan and she also dismisses the idea. She comments on his missing eye and asks if the woman he saved was worth the cost. Mat is shocked and asks how she knows, but she ignores the question. [[Furyk Karede|Karede]] arrives and offers his life to repay his shame. Tuon refuses, and tells him that the [[The Prince of the Ravens|Prince of Ravens]] will teach him how to spot a Gray Man. She dismisses everyone in order to spend time with Mat. She unceremoniously disrobes, still standing in the garden, and says that it is a reward for saving her life. Mat says he will not play her fool and if she just wants him to be her Toy, he will leave her. Mat asks if she loves him, but she replies she is with him because the omens say she must be. She concedes, however, that it is good to see him again. Mat accepts that for the time being.
